content:
Back in July, Apple rolled out a basic search feature update for its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely praised, but the same version of TestFlight also introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, this bug doesn't affect me much. So I view this TestFlight update as a small step, but a significant one.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users who have installed a large number of beta testing apps — Apple's latest TestFlight update is a clear example. Apple has just updated TestFlight across multiple platforms including iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The new version 4.3 adds a 'search bar for quickly finding apps'.

Looking back, I did notice something unusual at the time and noted it at the end of the article (although my judgment then was completely opposite to now):

The reason I didn't see it as a bug is that last year I merged two Apple accounts — one using iCloud and the other using the App Store — and kept the TestFlight app records accumulated over the years. The process wasn't exactly convenient, but I thought it was worth it.

In any case, the TestFlight bug was not overlooked — John Vorhees of MacStories discovered it:

So when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac mentioning that TestFlight finally has a search bar, you can imagine how excited I was. I thought: 'Finally!' and immediately dropped what I was doing to update the app. […] But there is a big 'however' here. Previously, TestFlight's beta tests were listed in reverse chronological order, which is exactly the way I liked it. […] Now, expired betas and still-valid betas are all mixed together in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a rough count — for me, there are close to 800 app records. As you'd expect, very few of these betas are actually useful. The search function does help, but you can no longer scroll through them one by one.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball discussing the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was raised by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, this update does indeed address the related bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is the fix provided for users affected by this regression issue.

Make the most of your Apple products
